steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.

Cream shortening and sugar together in a medium bowl; stir in pumpkin and vanilla. Sift flour, salt, baking soda, baking powder, and cinnamon together; stir into creamed mixture. Mix in butterscotch chips. Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes in preheated oven. Allow cookies to cool for a minute on cookie sheets before transferring to wire cooling racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Butterscotch Pumpkin Cookies
raw_recipe.description: Yummy pumpkin cookies with spices and butterscotch morsels. Moist, delicious, and perfect for fall.

review.reviewBody: Perfect cookie! To the reviewer that gave these a 4 our of 5 star because she wanted a crispier cookier and less cake like... if you have followed the recipe like it said you might have gotten what you wanted. Brown sugar will make a cookie softer. Please dont rate a recipe if you change it up and dont like what you did to it.... These cookies are perfect just follow the recipe.

This is not only a perfect pumpkin cookie but a perfect cookie in general. Every time I make these, they disappear and I'm asked for the recipe. I've been making these for 6 years now and the only thing I've added is 1/2tsp ground ginger and 1/8tsp nutmeg. Bake time 11-13 minutes. Bake on parchment lined airbake pans.

I wanted to make something quickly this morning to take home to my mom, but I hadn't been shopping this week so I was out of eggs, so most of my go-to recipes were out. I found a box of puréed pumpkin in my cabinet (similar to canned pumpkin, but a slightly more liquid texture). So I found this recipe and made a few alterations, and they can out perfect for what I wanted. I'm sure the original recipe is great on its own, but here's what I wanted - something soft and slightly cake-y, not too sugary bc my mom won't eat it then, and a bit of a kick, spice wise. I used 1/3 cup white sugar, 1/3 cup dark brown, thus reducing sugar by 1/3 cup. I also used 1 1/2 cup white I bleached all purpose flour, and 1/2 cup light brown all purpose flour (bc I ran out of white...I really need to go shopping). I used slightly more than a half cup of shortening (maybe an extra tablespoon), and slightly more than 1 tsp vanilla. I increased cinnamon by 1/4 tsp, added 1/4 tsp allspice, and 1/8 tsp ground cardamom. (If I didn't mention an ingredient, it's cause I didn't change the measurement from the original recipe). I omitted the butterscotch chips but added 2/3 cup chopped walnuts. I then lined my baking sheets with parchment paper and baked at 350 for exactly 10 minutes. It was perfect - not too sweet, soft, spicy, and pumpkiny! Also, I added chocolate chips to a couple of the cookies for myself, and that was delicious as well!

I don't know where you got this but it is my grandmas recipe ;) I have been making this for Thanksgiving and Christmas since I was old enough to bake. For people thinking these are too sweet or not pumpkin tasting enough, I add a couple teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice and cut back or cut out the cinnamon. I also add chopped walnuts with the butterscotch morsels. My favorite cookies ever. Note: pressed for time, I greased a 9 x 12 glass casserole dish and made these like bars last Christmas and every one loved them. You just have to change the amount of time in the oven. I am pretty sure it took at least twenty minutes. I kept pulling them out and adding five more minutes until a toothpick came out clean in the middle. Yum!!

Awesome! I used whole wheat flour (I always do), I used one teaspoon cinnamon, 1 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice and I used cinnamon chips. I took the advice on the shaping of the cookie prior to baking. They came out perfect! They are soft, cake-like cookies and everyone LOVED them. It seems to me these are Vegan without the cinnamon chips!? Oh, and they took about 16 minutes to bake.

These are soft cookies which will crisp a bit at the edges if you increase the baking time to around 10-12min. I substituted the butterscotch with semi-sweet chocolate chips and halved the sugar because other reviews said it was too sweet. I also added a teaspoon of pumpkin spice and tossed the cooled cookies in a bit of ground cinnamon to make up for decreased amount of sugar.

These were a big hit! I used chocolate chips instead of butterscotch, half butter/half shortening and added 1/8 t . of both nutmeg and ground cloves. Cooking time was longer, about 15 minutes. Will make them again.

I was looking for an eggless pumpkin cookie recipe for Thanksgiving and these did the trick. They were indeed very cake-like, moist, and light. Like others, I used brown sugar instead of white, and halved the butterscotch chips. I also added a 1/2 teaspoon of nutmeg because I am always looking for an excuse to use my favorite spice. 

I have mixed feelings about the butterscotch chips. I really love butterscotch, but definitely feel that the pumpkin played second fiddle here, even with the portion halved. If I wanted to make a super pumpkiny cookie I'd probably skip the butterscotch chips next time.

Oh, and having misread the recipe, I dropped them as tablespoonfuls and they still came out beautifully but had to cook for much longer, closer to 15 minutes. As they didn't spread or rise at all, I couldn't imagine them as teaspoon cookies--it seems they'd be tiny.

These are fantastic cookies, lightly pumpkiny and sweet with a great blend of flavors. The proportions are spot-on; mine made exactly the estimated 3 dozen. I added a little ginger and nutmeg as well, just a dash of each, and I recommend playing around with whatever spices you like in your pumpkin to get it just right for you! I also cut the chips back to 1 cup because as other reviewers have mentioned, butterscotch chips are quite sweet. If you like a very sweet cookie you will probably be fine with the given amount; if you like a little more flavor contrast, 1 cup is perfect. They needed 14 minutes in my oven; your mileage may vary. Just poke them with a toothpick, and if it doesn't come out doughy, they're done. I will be adding these to my fall recipe collection to make every year. Thanks for the great recipe!

Yes very nice soft mild cookie but could use a little kick, used my own pumking pie spice in place of cinn and could have used more. All in all will make again and tweek it. Used icecream scoop and flattened raw cookie with floured fork.

Substituted 1/2 cup butter for the shortening, used 1/2 cup sugar instead of the full cup, and added 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg, and ground cloves. The cookies turned out fantastic! My father in law loved them for his birthday. Woohoo!!

I made these for a party, and they got good compliments. My son said they were really good too. But I found the dough to be too greasy and rather tasteless. The butterscotch chips were the only flavor, and while they are yummy, I think the dough could be better. I was hoping they were vegan, but alas, butterscotch chips have milk solids. I will probably make them again with less Crisco, more pumpkin and maybe some applesauce (which are natural fat substitutes) and allspice. And I might reduce the qty of butterscotch chips so that flavor isn’t so overwhelming.
I make these every year during the fall. Made as directed. Used a cookie scoop and baked for 10-11 mins. They were very good. Soft and yummy.
So simple. So delicious 😋

Tasty. I used 1/3 cup brown sugar and 2/3 cup white sugar. Using the 8-10 minute recommendation, my cookies came out a little doughy in the middle. A couple more minutes is needed. 10-12 minutes would be more appropriate. But the flavor and the texture of the cookies are sublime.
Very good. They're really sweet and almost cake like.
Pretty bland. Followed as stated.
I use this recipe every fall season!
We used chocolate chips but they were moist and delicious
8 beautiful dozen
